newsitem.title: CANADA: CanOxy sees boosting '98 Yemen oil output.
newsitem.headline: CanOxy sees boosting '98 Yemen oil output.

text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd expects its share of oil production from the Masila Block in Yemen, where the company reported a big boost in reserves on Friday, to rise to 100,000 barrels a day next year, CanOxy spokesman Kevin Finn said.
"That's what I'm expecting to average next year," Finn said in a telephone interview. "And I don't see any significant drop in that for a number of years."

He also said further reserve increases were expected in the coming months from geological remapping and step-out drilling at existing fields, and from new discoveries such as the recently reported Dahban field.
In total, CanOxy and its partners expect to spend US$200 million-US$300 million over the next three years doubling the number of wells on the concession, he said.

The company reported on Friday that Masila production averaged a record 189,400 barrels a day -- 98,500 net to CanOxy -- and reached a one-day high of 210,000 barrels on June 25. Production comes from just 67 wells.
CanOxy's share of average output during last year's second quarter was 94,700 barrels a day.

It also said proved reserves on the play, in which CanOxy has a 52 percent stake, rose by 76 million barrels to 169 million barrels and its reserve life increased to five years from three years at the end of last year.
Rising production and reserves on the block over the past few years have come despite constant speculation among industry watchers that output was about to decline.
"When I went there, my comment was this thing's way bigger than people think it is," said Craig Langpap, analyst with Peters & Co. "I don't think you've seen the end of it."
Langpap said CanOxy, with the higher reserve tally, was demonstrating the fields within the block were larger than what was previously thought and recovery factors in the reservoirs were higher.
"The reserves that they initially recorded were very conservative," he said.

With a recent spate of Canadian oil companies failing to meet second-quarter production targets in western Canadian operations thanks to an unusally wet spring, the value of CanOxy's Yemen concession comes to the fore, he said.
Operating and administrative costs at Masila, at about US$1 a barrel, are also far lower than at home, Finn said.
Masila, which began pumping in 1993, produces about half of Yemen's total oil output.
CanOxy shares on Friday were down 0.15 to 35.60 in afternoon Toronto Stock Exchange trade. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
